analysis:
This PR changes only documentation: a new changelog fragment (changelog.d/delta-complete-checkpoints.md) and a three-line addition to docs/architecture/prefix-cache.md (head lines 545-547). No source code, crypto, authorization or attestation logic is in the supplied evidence, so no concrete regression can be shown.

The documented behavior is a feature: Qwen 3.8 recurrent complete checkpoints (native-paged-full-recurrent-v1 and native-contiguous-full-recurrent-v1) are written as deltas of the restored file, and a restore reads the chain forward. This is relevant to T-041 (SSD prefix-cache at-rest exposure, same-account TTFT oracle SEC-035), A-001, TB-007 and the encrypted DBK3 store.

Questions for whoever reviews the implementation, which is not in this batch:
(1) Each delta must be authenticated and bound to its parent: AAD, scope/cacheSalt, HMAC lookup tag, model/layout identity and epoch. A chain restore must not splice files across tenants or scopes, or accept a replaced or rolled-back parent.
(2) TTL and LRU eviction of a parent must not leave orphaned deltas that are mistakenly treated as restorable, and a missing parent must fall back cold.
(3) A chain may extend a file's effective lifetime beyond the 30-minute sliding TTL. Reading a chain forward should not slide TTL for files the request did not use authentically.
(4) Chain-restore read scratch, staging reservation and memory accounting must stay bounded, since a longer chain means more reads.
(5) Delta files must not add prompt-derived plaintext metadata (T-041 leak #2 class).
(6) The DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE_SSD_INCREMENTAL_CHECKPOINTS=0 kill switch should interact correctly with existing delta files. The doc says only that it restores complete files.

The changelog's performance claims (20.0 GB to 5.4 GB written, unchanged TTFT, identical outputs) are unverified here. I found no threat-model invalidation from the docs alone. The referenced anchor ../reference/ssd-kv-cache.md#delta-complete-checkpoints is not in the supplied evidence, so I flagged deeper review of the code that implements this.
